tone_statements.citation: Bayang Souloukna, Jules Paulin; Nounamou Dabou, Patrick; Dayang, Paul & Kolyang 2026. Acoustic and Tonal Modeling of the tpuri Language through a Multi-Modular Hybrid Approach. EAI Endorsed Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Machine Learning Applications 2 (published 2026-01-14), 13 pp. DOI 10.4108/eetismla.11285 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
tone_statements.quote: Tone. Tpuri is a tonal language: pitch patterns realised on syllables contribute to both lexical contrasts and grammatical distinctions. The system distinguishes six tones, four level (High, Mid-high, Mid-low, Low) and two contour tones (Rising and Falling). Tone interacts with morphology and syntax through phenomena such as tone spreading and tone sandhi, whereby the surface realisation of a tone depends on neighbouring tones and on prosodic phrasing.
tone_statements.locator: p. 4, §3.2 'Phonological Inventory', paragraph 'Tone'; TBU definition p. 8, §7 (tone error rate)
tone_statements.summary: Four level tones (H, MH, ML, L) plus rising and falling contours on vowel nuclei, lexical and grammatical function, with tone spreading/sandhi.

tone_statements.quote: Le tupuri est une langue à quatre hauteurs tonales. Les paires minimales sont imparfaites. Les consonnes obstruantes sonores et continues ont provoqué un abaissement tonal qui donne lieu à un ton infra-bas. Ce phénomène s’observe dans les formes verbales injonctives, où les verbes ayant une consonne sourde à l’initiale ont un schème tonal mi-haut mi-haut, tandis que les verbes à l’injonctif ayant des consonnes sonores à l’initiale ont le schéma infra-bas mi-haut. Le ton mi-bas provient de l’abaissement d’un ton mi-haut d’un schème mi-haut mi-bas. Les voyelles fermées après consonne sourde tendent à élever le registre mi-haut jusqu’à un registre haut.
tone_statements.translation: Tupuri is a language with four tone heights. Minimal pairs are imperfect. Voiced obstruents and continuants caused a tonal lowering that gives rise to an infra-low tone. This is observed in injunctive verb forms, where verbs with an initial voiceless consonant have a mid-high mid-high tone scheme, whereas injunctive verbs with initial voiced consonants have the scheme infra-low mid-high. The mid-low tone comes from the lowering of a mid-high tone in a mid-high mid-low scheme. Close vowels after a voiceless consonant tend to raise the mid-high register up to a high register.
tone_statements.summary: Four level tone heights (haut, mi-haut, mi-bas, bas) plus a derived infra-low from depressor (voiced obstruent/continuant) lowering; tone is lexical and grammatical (injunctive verb tone schemes); tones of elided final vowels merge onto the next syllable.

sources.note: First-hand precis by the main describer: 24 vowels, 25 consonants; 'langue à quatre hauteurs tonales' with imperfect minimal pairs; voiced obstruents and continuants caused tonal lowering yielding an infra-low tone, visible in injunctive verb forms (voiceless-initial verbs MH-MH vs voiced-initial infra-low-MH); mid-low derives from lowering of mid-high in a MH-ML scheme; close vowels after voiceless C raise MH toward H; French loan accent realised as H or MH tone by onset/vowel; tonal instability feeds consonantal instability in other dialects; morpho-tonology explains the creation of the fou…

sources.note: ASR paper with a language-description section (§3.2) and a tone-annotated 64 h corpus: Tpuri is tonal, tone lexical and grammatical, six tones = four level (High, Mid-high, Mid-low, Low) + two contours (Rising, Falling), tone spreading and sandhi; TBU = vowel nucleus, each annotated H/MH/ML/L/R/F (§7, p. 8); tone error rates per category (level tones lowest, contours highest). Also: 24 vowels (quality x nasality x length), length distinctive mainly in open syllables, lengthening as a correlate of contour tones (after Ruelland).
